title: Build mealie-pantry
prompt:
Build mealie-pantry, a small service that keeps our kitchen's pantry and tells us which of our Mealie recipes we can cook from it. This repository is empty apart from dev/, a stand-in for our Mealie API with sample data, for development (see dev/README.md).

Runtime
- Node.js 18 or later. `npm start` starts the HTTP server. Configuration comes from the environment: PORT (default 3000), MEALIE_URL (the base URL of the Mealie instance), DATABASE_PATH (the SQLite database file, default ./pantry.db). You may add npm dependencies.
- Storage is SQLite. The schema lives in plain SQL migration files in migrations/, named NNN_description.sql (001_init.sql, then 002_..., ...), applied in name order at startup and recorded in a schema_migrations table so that each runs once. Migrations are append-only: once one exists it is never edited; a schema change comes in a new file.
- Every response is JSON. Errors are {"error": "<message>"} with the status given below.

The Mealie API (read-only, as our instance serves it)
- GET {MEALIE_URL}/api/recipes?page=<n>&perPage=<n> returns {"page", "per_page", "total", "total_pages", "items": [{"id", "slug", "name", "tags": [{"name", "slug"}], "totalTime"}]}. A page may hold fewer items than asked for: read every page.
- GET {MEALIE_URL}/api/recipes/{slug} returns the recipe with "recipeIngredient": [{"quantity": number or null, "unit": {"name", "abbreviation"} or null, "food": {"name"} or null, "note": string}], or 404 when there is no such recipe.

Amounts
- An amount is a quantity of a food in a unit, recognised by its abbreviation. Amounts of one food add up within a kind of unit:
  - mass: g and kg, kept in grams, reported in "g" below 1000 g and otherwise in "kg";
  - volume: ml, l, tsp (5 ml), tbsp (15 ml) and cup (240 ml), kept in millilitres, reported in "ml" below 1000 ml and otherwise in "l";
  - no unit: a count, reported with unit null;
  - any other unit (a pinch, say): kept and reported under its abbreviation.
- Food names match case-insensitively and are reported in lower case. Reported quantities are rounded to 2 decimals.
- What a recipe needs: its ingredients summed per food and kind of unit. A null quantity counts as 1; an ingredient without a food is ignored.
- What the pantry lacks of a recipe's needs: for each food and kind, what it needs minus what the pantry holds, when that is above 0, reported like any amount. Lists of amounts are sorted by food, then by unit, null first.

Endpoints
- GET /health returns 200 {"ok": true}.
- POST /pantry/items with {"food": string, "quantity": number, "unit": string, or null or absent for a count} adds the amount and returns 201 with that food's total of that kind: {"food", "quantity", "unit"}. A missing or empty food, a quantity that is not a positive number, or a unit that is neither a string nor null is 400.
- GET /pantry returns 200 {"items": [{"food", "quantity", "unit"}]}: every food's total of every kind it is held in.
- DELETE /pantry/items/:food removes every amount of that food: 204, or 404 when the pantry has none. The food is URL-encoded.
- GET /recipes/cookable?maxMissing=<n> returns 200 {"recipes": [{"slug", "name", "missing": [{"food", "quantity", "unit"}]}]}: every Mealie recipe of which the pantry lacks at most n amounts (n from 0 to 20, default 0; anything else is 400), with what it lacks, sorted by the number of missing amounts and then by slug.
- POST /cook with {"slug"}: when the pantry lacks nothing the recipe needs, subtracts its needs (an amount that reaches 0 leaves the pantry) and returns 200 {"slug", "items": [the pantry afterwards, as GET /pantry lists it]}. Otherwise it returns 409 {"error", "missing": [what it lacks]} and changes nothing. A recipe Mealie does not know is 404; a missing slug is 400.

Write tests for it. The service is done when it implements all of the above.
